tieu_de: How to read your birth chart in 10 steps
mo: Run the steps on your own chart

A birth chart has around 40 things in it: ten planets, twelve signs, twelve houses, a few dozen aspects, several angles. Most people open one, see the wheel, and close it. The problem isn't the chart. It's that nobody told them the order to look in.

This is that order. Ten steps, each one building on the last, each with a "what to write down" so you end up with a page of notes instead of a headache. Budget an hour the first time. After that it takes ten minutes.

doan: Count elements and modalities
Find the angular planets
Find the tightest aspects
Write the one-paragraph summary
Planet Sun Rules Leo Ego, will, vitality
Planet Moon Rules Cancer Emotions, intuition, nurturing
Point Ascendant U Planet Saturn Rules Capricorn Discipline, responsibility, structure
Planet Venus Rules Taurus, Libra Love, beauty, values
Planet Mars Rules Aries Action, energy, desire

Before anything else, know how good the time is. To the minute: read everything. Within an hour: read the rising sign as likely, not certain. Unknown: skip steps 3 and 5, treat houses as unknown, and put the rest of your attention on signs and aspects.
Write down: "time reliable / approximate / unknown."

Sun sign, Moon sign, rising sign. The Sun is your core and direction, the Moon your needs and reflexes, the rising sign your front door. Read a short description of each and note where they agree and where they pull apart.
The pull-apart is the interesting part. Aries Sun with a Cancer Moon wants to charge and needs to feel safe. That tension is more "you" than either sign alone.
Write down: the three signs, and one sentence about the tension between them.

Take the rising sign, find the planet that rules it (Aries: Mars, Taurus and Libra: Venus, Gemini and Virgo: Mercury, Cancer: Moon, Leo: Sun, Scorpio: Mars or Pluto, Sagittarius: Jupiter, Capricorn: Saturn, Aquarius: Saturn or Uranus, Pisces: Jupiter or Neptune). Now find that planet in your chart. Its house is where your life keeps going. Its sign is how.
A Leo rising with the Sun in the 6th house: warm front door, but the life is about work, service, and health. Same Leo rising with the Sun in the 11th: the life is about groups, friends, causes.
Write down: the ruler, its sign and house, one sentence.
Tally the planets by element (fire, earth, air, water) and mode (cardinal, fixed, mutable). Give the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant extra weight. Look for anything heavy (five or more) or missing (zero).

A missing element is the most useful finding: it's what you'll compensate for or look for in other people. No earth: money and the body take conscious effort. No water: feelings take conscious effort.
Write down: heavy and missing, if any.

Look at the four angles: Ascendant (left), Descendant (right), Midheaven (top), IC (bottom). Any planet within about 8 degrees of an angle is angular, and angular planets are loud regardless of what they are.

Saturn on the Ascendant makes the person serious. Jupiter on the Midheaven makes the career big. Neptune on the IC makes home hard to pin down. If you have an angular planet, it's often the first thing an astrologer would mention.
Write down: any angular planets and which angle.

Go to the aspect list and sort by orb. The three tightest aspects (under 2 degrees, ideally) are the ones that shape the chart most. Note whether each is hard (square, opposition) or soft (trine, sextile) or a conjunction.
Then check specifically for aspects to the Sun, Moon, and chart ruler. Anything touching those three carries extra weight even at a wider orb.
Write down: the three tightest aspects, and any hard aspect to the Sun or Moon.
Three or more planets forming a shape:
Stellium: three or more planets in one sign or house. That area dominates.
T-square: two planets in opposition, both square a third. The third planet is the pressure point and the engine.
Grand trine: three planets in a triangle, same element. Natural talent, easy to coast on.
Grand cross: four planets in two oppositions crossing. Rare, demanding, productive.
Yod: two planets sextile, both quincunx a third. A "finger" pointing at an adjustment the person has to make.
The chart tool marks these for you. If you have one, it usually explains a lot of the tightest aspects from step 6.
Write down: any pattern and its focal planet.

Venus is how you love and what you want. Mars is how you go after it and how you fight. Read the sign of each, and the house if the time is good. Then check whether they aspect each other: a Venus-Mars square is desire that doesn't quite line up with affection; a trine is the two working together.
This step is short but it's the one people ask about most, so it deserves its own line.
Write down: Venus sign and house, Mars sign and house, the aspect between them if any.
Saturn's house is where you feel inadequate early and become an authority late. Saturn's sign is the style of the lesson. Saturn's aspects to personal planets show what it puts the brakes on.

Saturn in the 7th: relationships are slow and serious and get better with age. Saturn square the Sun: confidence has to be earned, and is. Everyone has Saturn somewhere; reading it early stops it from being a surprise at 29.
Write down: Saturn's house, and its tightest aspect to a personal planet.
Now put it together. From your notes, write four or five sentences:
Who this person is (Big Three and the tension)
Where their energy goes (chart ruler's house, angular planets)
What they're working with (tightest aspects, pattern, missing element)
How they love (Venus, Mars)
What they're building slowly (Saturn)

Example, for a real chart: "Aries Sun, Cancer Moon, Virgo rising: a fighter who needs to feel safe and comes across as careful. Mercury rules the chart and sits in the 8th house, so the life keeps going toward deep, private, uncomfortable subjects. No air in the chart: this person feels and acts more than they explain. Sun square Saturn (1 degree) is the main lesson: confidence built through failure. Venus in Pisces in the 7th wants a soulmate; Mars in Capricorn in the 5th plays the long game with creative work and children. Saturn in the 4th: home is the thing they build, slowly, and eventually own."
That paragraph is a reading. Not a professional one, but a real one, and it came from the chart in a fixed order rather than from a list of sign descriptions.

doan: Open the birth chart tool → . Every step above maps to a panel: the Big Three and angles are on the wheel, the chart ruler and elements are in the sidebar, the Aspects tab sorts by orb, and the Patterns section marks stelliums, T-squares, and grand trines.

Do it once for yourself, then once for someone you know well. The second chart is where you'll find out whether the method works, because you already know the answer and can see whether the chart got there.
